analysis:
Examined both files' metadata, all supplied patches and text, including the complete BASE cache reference. The changes describe retaining a whole-read encrypted buffer rather than copying it (changelog.d/ssd-read-single-copy.md HEAD 3–8; docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md HEAD patch line 65), plus an update date. No executable implementation is supplied in this batch, so the documentation establishes no concrete security regression.
Against T-041, A-001 and TB-007, the documented optimization does not alter AES-GCM authentication, HMAC naming/account scope, TTL, key custody or purge rules. Surrounding BASE documentation retains authenticated chunks and EOF/file-identity checks (65), bounded staging (99–104), host IO lifetime (126), retry byte charging before allocation/read including partial reads (278), and fail-closed identity binding (294–306). No changes to authorization, attestation, wire encryption, billing or privileged/local-control boundaries are evidenced here; existing limitations are not new findings.
Integration must inspect provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/KVCacheSSD/SSDBlockStore.swift readExactly and its changed tests: verify exact-length handling for whole, partial, empty and truncated reads; preservation of pre-read budget checks and size bounds; and buffer ownership/indexing through SSDBlockChunkCursor.swift and SSDBlockStore+Streaming.swift. Confirm authentication and file-identity checks remain authoritative and read/decrypt aliases retire before host reservation refund. The claimed lower-copy behavior and timing measurements alone cannot establish these contracts. Remaining uncertainty is implementation coverage, not an observed missing control.
